title: Energy Engineers, Except Wind and Solar
description: Design, develop, or evaluate energy-related projects or programs to reduce energy costs or improve energy efficiency during the designing, building, or remodeling stages of construction. May specialize in electrical systems; heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning (HVAC) systems; green buildings; lighting; air quality; or energy procurement.

tasks.text: Conduct energy audits to evaluate energy use and to identify conservation and cost reduction measures.
Monitor and analyze energy consumption.
Inspect or monitor energy systems, including heating, ventilating, and air conditioning (HVAC) or daylighting systems to determine energy use or potential energy savings.
Collect data for energy conservation analyses, using jobsite observation, field inspections, or sub-metering.
Research renewable or alternative energy systems or technologies, such as solar thermal or photovoltaic energy.
Identify and recommend energy savings strategies to achieve more energy-efficient operation.
Verify energy bills and meter readings.
Review architectural, mechanical, or electrical plans or specifications to evaluate energy efficiency.
Analyze, interpret, or create graphical representations of energy data, using engineering software.
Perform energy modeling, measurement, verification, commissioning, or retro-commissioning.
Prepare energy-related project reports or related documentation.
Write or install energy management routines for building automation systems.
Monitor energy related design or construction issues, such as energy engineering, energy management, or sustainable design.
Advise clients or colleagues on topics such as climate control systems, energy modeling, data logging, sustainable design, or energy auditing.

Manage the development, design, or construction of energy conservation projects to ensure acceptability of budgets and time lines, conformance to federal and state laws, or adherence to approved specifications.
Review or negotiate energy purchase agreements.
Train personnel or clients on topics such as energy management.
Direct the implementation of energy management projects.
Promote awareness or use of alternative or renewable energy sources.
Recommend best fuel for specific sites or circumstances.
Consult with construction or renovation clients or other engineers on topics such as Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design (LEED) or Green Buildings.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Systems Analysis
skills.def: Determining how a system should work and how changes in conditions, operations, and the environment will affect outcomes.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Mathematics
skills.def: Using mathematics to solve problems.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Science
skills.def: Using scientific rules and methods to solve problems.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Systems Evaluation
skills.def: Identifying measures or indicators of system performance and the actions needed to improve or correct performance, relative to the goals of the system.

skills.name: Operations Analysis
skills.def: Analyzing needs and product requirements to create a design.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.def: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.

skills.name: Instructing
skills.def: Teaching others how to do something.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Object or component oriented development software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications using object-oriented programming concepts. Examples: C++, Python, R.

skills.name: Analytical or scientific software
skills.def: Software to capture data, perform analysis, or generate reports or visualizations to support scientific research. Examples: 360 Analytics eQUEST, AIRMaster+, Architectural Energy Corporation ENFORMA Building Diagnostics, Architectural Energy Corporation VisualDOE.

skills.name: Computer aided design CAD software
skills.def: Software to design 2D or 3D objects. May include engineering or architectural features. Examples: Autodesk AutoCAD, Home Energy Efficient Design HEED.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Presentation software
skills.def: Software to create presentations, speeches, or slideshows. Examples: Microsoft PowerPoint.
